newsitem.title: UK: Channel Tunnel has first passenger train since fire.
newsitem.headline: Channel Tunnel has first passenger train since fire.

text.p: The first Eurostar high-speed passenger train to use the Channel Tunnel since a fire two weeks ago left London on Wednesday, but with no fare-paying passengers on board, the company said.
The Paris-bound train left London's Waterloo station at 0600 GMT carrying only crew, journalists and a public relations officer.
Eurotunnel SA/Plc employees had been working around the clock to reopen the tunnel after a blaze on a truck-carrying wagon on November 18.
Eurostar spokesman Roger Harrison said it would take up to half an hour longer than the usual 20 minutes for the train to pass through the tunnel.
He said another train was scheduled to leave Paris for London at 0610 GMT.
Eurotunnel hopes to run two thirds of normal passenger and freight traffic in the next three to six months while repairs are completed, Eurotunnel spokesman Francois Borel said.
